phrase: Before we close — who is doing what and by when?
Let us confirm the next action: [who] will do [what] by [when].
The next step is X, and [Name] owns it by [date].
To make this concrete: I will do X by Thursday.
Can we name the one thing that needs to happen before we next meet?
Who is taking the first action from this conversation?
I want to close with a clear next step — is that [X]?
Does everyone agree that is the next step?
Are you comfortable committing to that timeline?
Any blockers to making that happen?
Should I send a summary of that so it is in writing?
Does that feel like a reasonable next step?
So — who does what by when?
Next step?
Who owns this one?
What date shall we put on that?
First action: mine or yours?
What happens next, and who makes it happen?
This needs one owner — who is it?
I need a name against that action, not a 'we'.
A date, please — 'soon' has let us down before.
If nobody owns this by the end of the call, it will not happen.
I will take it — and I need your draft by Tuesday to do it.
Let us not leave until that has an owner and a deadline.
I do not want this to become one of those 'we must catch up' promises — shall we pick a date now?
Let us make it real: dinner, Thursday, ours?
I loved this — can we book the next one before we forget?
You mentioned needing help with the move — name a day and I am there.
Rather than 'sometime soon', how about Saturday?
I will text you tomorrow to lock it in — that way we actually do it.
